title: How AI Agents Let GTM Teams Scale — Justin Joyce, Cloudflare
talk_summary: Cloudflare's GTM ops team built role-specific skill files, a draft-reviewer-tone multi-agent workflow, and a self-service agent workspace to scale analysis and insight. The transferable lessons are curated skills, explicit reviewer agents, per-call observability, pre-engineered context, and feedback loops rather than GTM-specific tactics.

takeaways.technique: Role-specific skill files with embedded business logic
takeaways.what_they_do: They build skill files containing business context tied to data, plus tested common question types, so non-technical users can query data without SQL bottlenecks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have built role-specific skill files, which have the context of the business information tying it to the data

takeaways.what_they_do: A first agent drafts using MCP data, a second reviewer agent checks data veracity, and a third tone agent formats risks and opportunities consistently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a second reviewer agent who checks the veracity of the data, and then we have a third um agent, which is a tone agent

takeaways.what_they_do: They log every LLM call input and response and inspect every run during a multi-month test to find what is going wrong.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with every run, we have observability into each of the LLM calls, so we can see what is passed and what is the response

takeaways.what_they_do: They transform data by time, business slice, and metric and embed filtering/aggregation logic upfront so agents analyze clean, consistent data.
Skills are presented through a central alias, curated by ops and GTM teams, and reviewed to prevent skill proliferation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they're reviewed, so we can make sure that we're not having a proliferation of skills

takeaways.technique: Internal feedback loop on agent usefulness
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat internal agent users like customers and collect feedback on whether outputs are useful and what issues they hit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the feedback loop is very important to be able to see is is what you're building is it actually useful?
